project.name: Sequence Growth
project.description: Natural-division recurrence bounds and eventual exponential domination for sequences of natural numbers.

review.notes: The two listed recurrence theorems and their documented hypotheses have been independently agent-reviewed; no complete coverage of an external source is asserted.

automation.notes: Formal Frontier Agents developed the Lean proofs with AI assistance and reused Mathlib's arithmetic foundations.

headlines.title: `Nat.DivisionGrowth.affine_lower_bound`
headlines.text:
If `0 < s < n` and
`∀ m, n * (u m / s) ≤ u (m + 1)`, then for every `m : ℕ`, with
`λ = (n : ℚ) / s` and `C = (n : ℚ) * ((s - 1 : ℕ) : ℚ) / ((n : ℚ) - s)`,
`λ ^ m * ((u 0 : ℚ) - C) + C ≤ (u m : ℚ)`. There is **no** seed condition.

headlines.title: `Nat.DivisionGrowth.eventually_dominates`
headlines.text:
Under the same recurrence,
`0 < s`, `0 < b`, `s * b < n`, and the sufficient natural seed
`n * (s - 1) < (n - s) * u 0`, for **each** `K : ℕ` there is `M : ℕ`
such that **every** `m ≥ M` satisfies `K * b ^ m < u m`.

The seed is sufficient, not necessary. See [the mathematical guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/sequence-growth/blob/ccf81c7190cb1da914c71efaa20689c0e1d7ab62/docs/DivisionGrowth.md)
for the precise Lean signatures, the rational shift, examples and boundary cases.
